outcomes.text: Identify and describe needs or opportunities for design and technological improvement.
Analyse problems and create design specifications for identified needs.
Identify constraints from knowledge, resources and external factors that may affect proposed solutions.
Collect, organise and evaluate information relevant to practical and technological problems.
Produce or interpret data using diagrams, flow charts, graphs, experiments and test results.
Generate and record potential solutions using varied design techniques.
Identify the resources required to solve practical or technological problems.
Use varied media and equipment to make models and mock-ups for exploration and feasibility testing.
Continuously review personal progress, thinking and decisions during design work.
Relate self-assessment decisions to the study purpose and personal specification.
Extract, interpret and record relevant information and data from sources.
Research existing products, including through internet use.
Recognise design and technology’s effects on social, environmental and economic issues.
Understand the roles of designers, artisans and technologists in industry and society.
Consider a range of human needs when designing.
Consider how existing products satisfy users’ needs.
Understand the importance of anthropometrics and ergonomics.
Recognise fossil-fuel, nuclear and renewable energy sources.
Understand finite and nearly unlimited energy sources and how design can conserve them.
Recognise designers’ responsibilities for sustainable materials and resources.
Understand why recycling is necessary.
Identify recyclable and non-recyclable materials using product recycling symbols.
Understand why products should be designed for disassembly and component reuse.
Understand that products can be designed with deliberately limited lifetimes.
Choose and develop a solution after considering time, cost, skills and available resources.
Plan production of the selected solution in detail.
Recognise correct procedures for preparing materials.
Recognise accurate methods for drawing, marking out and testing.
Select suitable processes for shaping, forming, cutting, joining, fitting, assembling and finishing materials.
Recognise correct use of hand tools, machine tools and equipment.
Understand the need for required safety precautions with tools, machines, materials and resources.
Understand designers’ responsibility for ensuring products are safe to use.
Understand the importance of protecting personal safety and the safety of others.
Recognise basic workshop safety symbols.
Use technical language, numerical skills and visual media to communicate design ideas precisely and clearly.
Understand CAD/CAM benefits for designing and manufacturing individual or batch products.
Understand how CAD generates two-dimensional and three-dimensional images.
Understand industrial applications of CAD/CAM.
Recognise computer-controlled machines, including CNC mills, routers, engravers, lathes and laser cutters.
Understand how computers improve stock control and quality control.
Understand one-off, batch and mass production.
Generate proposals by identifying resources, planning manufacture and evaluating against specifications.
Use energy sources effectively and efficiently.
Choose materials using environmental and sustainability criteria.
Evaluate existing products and systems, other people’s work and personal work.
Test product or solution performance against its original specification.
Use varied methods and sources, such as surveys and interviews, to judge product effectiveness.
Propose improvements considering function, safety, appearance, ergonomics and cost.
Understand how function and aesthetics influence solutions and the work of others.
Use models to test design proposals.
Identify input devices, processing elements, output devices and feedback within control systems.
Understand physical and working properties of plastics, woods and metals and their applications.
Understand smart and modern materials, including thermochromic materials, polymorph, SMA and shape-memory polymer.
Know the main thermoplastic and thermosetting plastics and their common applications.
Know natural timber classifications, properties and uses.
Understand timber seasoning and appropriate storage and construction care.
Understand timber steaming, bending and adhesive curing times and strengths.
Know plywood, blockboard, chipboard, hardboard and MDF.
Compare the advantages and disadvantages of manufactured boards with solid wood.
Know common ferrous and non-ferrous metals and their alloys.
Understand how work hardening, annealing, case hardening, hardening and tempering alter material structure and suitability.
Understand composites and practical uses of Kevlar, CFRP and GRP.
Know available market forms, types and sizes of materials.
Understand cutting with hacksaws, guillotines, saws and portable power tools.
Understand datum surfaces, lines and edges and create them by planing or filing.
Explain machine-process preparation and safe methods for securing materials.
Measure and mark materials using appropriate rules, gauges, squares, punches, dividers, calipers and templates.
Produce datum lines using a surface plate, scribing block or calipers.
Measure accurately with micrometers, vernier gauges or digital calipers.
Understand bending, casting, lamination, vacuum forming, blow moulding, injection moulding, extrusion and press forming.
Select and perform suitable cutting, material-removal, joining and material-addition processes to create required shapes.
Use fabrication and fitting methods to join product parts permanently or temporarily.
Understand soldering, brazing, welding, riveting and pop riveting.
Understand carcase, stool and frame construction using permanent and temporary joints.
Use holding devices, formers and jigs to support sawing, drilling, bending, joining and assembly.
Understand knock-down fittings for manufactured boards, including corner blocks, scan fittings, cam locks and leg fastenings.
Understand applications for screws, nails, nuts, bolts, hinges and catches.
Understand how screws, nails, nuts and bolts are sized.
Recognise adhesives for different materials and requirements for preparation, application, drying and safety.
Understand preparation and application of surface treatments.
Recognise finishes including oils, paints, lacquers, stains, satin polishes and dip coatings.
Recognise surface finishes suitable for interior and exterior applications.
Recognise finishes that prevent corrosion or stains or withstand heat and liquids.
Understand self-finishing materials and how they achieve their surfaces.
Understand electroplating and anodising.
Identify and classify natural and manufactured structures found in everyday settings.
Describe and compare structural materials used in beams, frames, arches and cables.
Recognise frames and identify how triangulation provides rigidity.
Explain tension, compression, shear, bending, torsion and static loads in structural design.
Identify and sketch first-, second- and third-order levers with their linkages.
Choose spur gears for practical applications using relevant selection factors.
Explain ways to reduce friction through design, lubrication and other suitable methods.
Recognise and give examples of rotary, linear, reciprocating and oscillating motion.
Draw circuit diagrams using correct electronic symbols and conventions.
Distinguish between series and parallel component connections.
Compare conductivity and insulation when choosing materials.
Use units and prefixes for measuring current, voltage, resistance and capacitance.
Explain the operation and uses of toggle, push-button, micro and reed switches.
Design and make working models or products using resistant materials, components and kits.
Design, make and evaluate a static structure.
Define a moment as force multiplied by distance, measured in newton-metres.
Use moments in simple beam and lever loading calculations.
Explain how structures withstand stress and stationary or moving loads.
Draw, describe and identify beams, struts, ties and other structural members.
Explain how member length, cross-sectional shape and material affect performance.
Select and use joints for solid and hollow materials.
Select and use gussets, ribs, braces and laminations for reinforcement.
Apply equilibrium when considering applied loads and structural reactions.
Use stress and strain relationships involving force, area and changes in length.
Explain the factor of safety and its importance in structural design.
Explain and use load, effort, fulcrum, mechanical advantage, velocity ratio and efficiency.
Apply lever principles to design and make a simple machine.
Select bevel, worm, rack-and-pinion and other gears for practical applications.
Select flat, toothed, round and vee belt systems, sprockets, chains and tensioning systems.
Calculate simple gear ratios and transmission speeds.
Determine mechanical advantage, velocity ratio, efficiency and rotation direction for specified mechanisms.
Compare plain, roller and ball bearings and match them to operating conditions.
Explain crank, cam, follower, dwell, stroke, screw thread and pitch.
Compare and select mechanisms that convert motion between different types.
Use Ohm’s law to calculate current-limiting resistor values.
Measure current, voltage and resistance with ammeters, voltmeters and multimeters.
Calculate electrical power using P = VI.
Design and construct printed circuit boards.
Use soldering, suitable tools and other connection methods.
Apply health and safety procedures when building circuits.
Explain NC, NO, SPST and DPDT switch and relay terminology.
Use relays to switch higher-voltage circuits for motors and solenoids.
Construct and draw relay circuits for motor reversal and latched switching.
Read resistor colour codes to determine value and tolerance, then select a suitable resistor.
Draw and calculate series and parallel resistor circuits.
Calculate resistance and voltage in potential-divider circuits.
Describe transistor amplification from base current to collector-emitter current.
Identify when NPN bipolar transistors should be used as circuit switches.
Explain diode one-way conduction and protection against relay back electromotive force.
Use LEDs and calculate a suitable protective current-limiting resistor.
Explain the function of seven-segment displays.
Explain applications of LDRs and thermistors.
Distinguish between polarised and non-polarised capacitors and their applications.
Construct and draw monostable and astable 555-timer circuits.
Explain how programmable integrated circuits can provide time delays.
Calculate time delays using a supplied formula.
Use AND, OR, NAND, NOR and NOT gates with truth tables in simple control systems.
Demonstrate knowledge of 4000-series integrated circuits.
Use an operational amplifier to compare voltages.
Give everyday examples of logic-control systems.
Draw isometric views of circles, arcs and other curves.
Draw planometric views at 45° × 45° and 60° × 30°, including circles and arcs.
Construct accurate ellipses, including with a trammel.
Use thin and thick lines, shading, texture and colour rendering to communicate form and materials.
Choose suitable presentation methods for particular purposes.
Draw diagrams and lettering suited to the information, purpose and intended user.
Demonstrate lettering effects using styles, spacing, transfers, stencils and computer-generated text.
Describe commercial printing methods including gravure, screen printing and lithography.
Use computers to research shapes, images and fonts.
Use computers to resize shapes, images and lettering for graphic products.
Understand how digital images can be captured and stored on computers.
Recognise how CAD and CAM support drawing and manufacturing.
Recognise computer output devices that produce hard copies or cut profiles.
